thread.title: The Growth Scare: Put Your Emotions Aside And Start Buying For 2019 Gains - SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (NYSEARCA:SPY) | Seeking Alpha

author: Hawkinvest
title: The Growth Scare: Put Your Emotions Aside And Start Buying For 2019 Gains - SPDR S&P 500 Trust ETF (NYSEARCA:SPY) | Seeking Alpha
text:
Obviously there has been a lot going on with the market lately, and while many of us are upset to see stock prices decline, it is important to remember that market corrections also bring some of the best buying opportunities.
I believe the selloff is overdone based on the economic fundamentals. To me it appears that we had a market that had downward momentum, and when the Fed did not say exactly what the market wanted to hear, it sparked another round of tax-loss and margin call selling pressure at a time of year that is lacking liquidity. It also does not help that we are facing a government shutdown, even though these have historically been non-events. I also blame algorithmic trading for exacerbating downside moves, especially at a time when there is limited liquidity in the market due to the holidays.
In hindsight, I believe this market correction will just be thought of as a big growth scare and a buying opportunity. We had a similar correction in early 2018, and it did not take long for the market to resume an upward path. GDP growth is likely to be slower in 2019, when compared to 2018, but that does not mean growth is gone. I don't think the Fed will raise rates twice in 2019, and that should help the market in the coming year. I also think there are some positives: much cheaper oil which could act like a major tax cut for businesses and consumers. Speaking of taxes, it seems that many taxpayers did not adjust their withholding levels in 2018, and this means that tax refunds could be larger than ever. That could result in strong consumer spending in early 2019, as well as more money for the stock market with regular and retirement account contributions. The market could now be poised to climb a "wall of worry" in 2019, especially from the much lower level that it sits at now. The big market worries which include an overly aggressive Fed, concerns over Brexit, and tariffs against China are all man-made and can and will be resolved.
The global economy did not surge when Britain joined the European Union and it will not collapse when and if it leaves. The best thing would be for the bandage to be ripped off quickly, rather than this belabored process. A resolution either way could be a big relief, and maybe Brexit will be about as fierce as Y2K. Governments and companies have had plenty of time to prepare and make adjustments and contingency plans for Brexit, so it is going to be one of the least surprising "surprises", if it happens.
Ironically, the Fed is trying to raise rates so that it can lower rates. I think Jerome Powell could have sent a clearer message to the markets because he said the Fed would be data dependent and that the Fed forecasts just two rate hikes for 2019, instead of three. He also said that the Fed expects slower growth in 2019. It makes little sense to raise rates when growth is expected to slow, especially when we are in the later stages of an economic cycle. There is also a lag time for interest rate hikes to impact the real economy, so after the December rate hike, it seems overly aggressive to not just simply say we are done raising rates for now, unless the data warrants additional rate hikes for 2019. I don't think the Fed is going to be in a position to raise rates twice in 2019, and when the market becomes more focused on that, we could see a major relief rally. Just after the December rate hike, some Fed members immediately spoke out to reassure the markets that it will not keep raising rates, if it is not warranted. This alone should allow the market to calm down soon over the fears that the Fed was poised to continue with an overly aggressive path in 2019.
Another major relief rally can come when a deal with China is made. This will remove uncertainty and boost global growth as well as oil prices, and that will lift stocks. There are already signs that China is willing to make changes as they recently agreed to significantly reduce tariffs on U.S. made cars. While this trade dispute is causing some short-term pain, it could bring some long-term gains.
As I mentioned earlier, it appears that the selloff has been overdone and exacerbated because of the holiday season. At this time of year, there is less liquidity in the market and that means downward moves are likely exaggerated and probably not sustainable for too long. The CNN Money Fear and Greed Index is now at 3 which is about as low as it can go. The 3 level that represents "extreme fear" and "extreme greed" is reached when the index is close to 100. Warren Buffett says it is wise to be "Fearful when others are greedy and greedy when others are fearful". We are all getting a chance to buy now as extreme fear levels are clearly evident. I am not saying to go all in, but it makes sense to avoid emotion and exercise the discipline to buy when there is this level of fear in the market.
Source: CNN Money
The market is deeply oversold now which means it could be like a coiled spring and possibly due for a big rebound day or week. As the chart of the S&P 500 Index ( SPY ) below shows, the relative Strength Index or "RSI" is now around 19, which puts it deeply into oversold territory.
Some of the most beat up sectors at year end are likely to be the best performing in 2019. I think it makes sense to buy tech stocks like Apple ( AAPL ) since it is much cheaper than it was just a few weeks ago. Investor concerns about iPhone sales will probably fade next year, especially as investors consider a massive upgrade cycle that 5G phones could bring in 2020. I think the current share price and pessimism about iPhone sales is not warranted when you consider the growth of services, the Apple Watch, and the focus on health applications in the future. I have no doubt that there are other secret plans and products that will be announced in the future. Gene Munster, a well known analyst who has been right about Apple stock for years, predicts the share price can hit $350 in 3 years . Historically, it has always paid off to buy Apple shares on dips and when there were concerns about slowing iPhone sales, as there are now.
Many small cap stocks are also looking very undervalued now and could be poised for big rebounds as tax-loss selling is about to end. My top pick for a rebound into January is U.S. Xpress ( USX ) which went public earlier this year at $16 per share and now trades for just around $5 per share. Investor concerns about the economy have caused a vicious sell-off in the transports sector and that, along with tax-loss selling and a market correction, has taken this freight company to oversold levels. Analysts expect this company to earn $1.25 for this fiscal year. On November 1, it reported a quarterly profit of 33 cents per share. This missed estimates of 36 cents per share which caused the stock to drop in a weak market, but how many $5 stocks are earning even 33 cents per share in a single quarter? For the next fiscal year, analyst estimates are $1.55 per share which means this stock is now trading for just over 3 times forward earnings. On November 2, 2018, BofA/Merrill reiterated a buy rating but lowered the price target from $20 to $15. JPMorgan gave this stock an " overweight rating" and set a $15 price target for this stock on November 2, 2018. Both of these analyst moves reflect the most recent earnings report from the company, so both of these $15 price targets are based on the latest financials from the company.
In summary: Everyone wants to buy stocks at lower prices until they actually get the chance to do so. The fears about an aggressive Fed and slower growth appear way overdone. The markets have successfully dealt with a divided U.S. Government and problems in Europe for years and managed to climb a wall of worry. Extreme levels of fear and deeply oversold conditions also suggests that investors should be buying stocks now, and certainly not selling.
